title: Low Tide: After the Storm
statement: Halvard asked, and lost, for a storm tide to reach the dune. The dune lost anyway. One night the sea came all the way up over Mara's grass, flattened a wide stretch of it into combed sand, and left a new wrack line far above the old ones, at the dune's foot, thick and dark and full of what a storm carries: the weed, yes, and fourteen pieces of orange plastic that did not come from any beach. The seven older lines are still there below, the transect pegs are presumably still there under the sand. A beach turning into ground was interrupted; it will start again from a higher line. The next hand can pick the plastic out, or wait for the grass.
process: I kept Mara's parent exactly, the fresh kelp, the six ghost lines, the burrows, the grass and the rising dune, flattened a stretch of the grass under a pale wash of combed sand, and added a new thick dark wrack line high on the beach with a pale wet edge, a dashed debris line and fourteen small orange fragments scattered along it.
